newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to make radio address on Belarus accord.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to make radio address on Belarus accord.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will deliver a radio address on Saturday to explain Russia's planned union with neighbouring Belarus, a Kremlin spokesman said on Friday.

"The theme of his speech will be -- formation of a union between Russia and Belarus, its tasks, problems and prospectives," the spokesman said, adding the speech would be broadcast at 11 a.m. (0700 GMT).

Yeltsin and Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko signed a Union Treaty on Wednesday. But the document was considerably watered down compared to the original draft after hectic last minute behind-the-scenes negotiations.

The changes appeared to reflect pressure from liberal critics in Russia who feared the original draft could harm Russia's economy and make the hardline Lukashenko, who has been pressing hard for a close union with Russia, a key player in Moscow politics.

Lukashenko, who used a landslide win at a referendum last November to shut down parliament and seize vastly wider powers, has cracked down on opponents and the media, drawing widespread criticism in the West especially in Washington.
An unsanctioned opposition protest in Minsk to mark the signing of the Union Treaty ended in clashes on Wednesday in which a number of people were injured.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, told Interfax news agency the president was following events in Belarus closely and was aware of liberal concerns over human rights and freedoms there.

"The president states firmly that the Russian side will do everything to ensure that democracy, freedom of speech and of the press become a common asset of our union with Belarus," Yastrzhembsky said.
